[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-005-machine-readable-agent-specification-pattern.md#problem-statement]

### Problem Statement

AI agents assigned to a work task require structured, unambiguous context to produce reliable, standards-compliant output. Human-authored work items — user stories, issue descriptions, task notes — are written for human cognition: they contain implicit domain assumptions, colloquial language, and incomplete constraint references that a human engineer resolves through experience and conversation. An AI agent has none of that implicit resolution capability. Without a deliberate specification format that serves both human and machine readers, agent output quality is non-deterministic and degrades as task complexity increases.
page_texts.5:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-005-machine-readable-agent-specification-pattern.md#solution-overview]

### Solution Overview

The Machine-Readable Agent Specification Pattern defines a structured template for work items that are intended for autonomous AI agent execution. The template enforces three required sections — **Goal**, **Acceptance Criteria**, and **Constraints** — that give an agent a complete, parseable, self-contained task definition. The template is stored as an issue tracker template (e.g., via `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/`) so that the structure is enforced at authoring time rather than reviewed post-hoc. The spec is simultaneously human-readable for engineers and product owners, and machine-parseable for agent pipelines.
page_texts.6:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-005-machine-readable-agent-specification-pattern.md#when-to-use]

### When to Use

- When a work item will be assigned to an AI agent for autonomous or semi-autonomous execution
- When building agent pipeline infrastructure that requires deterministic context injection
- When establishing team standards for AI-executable work item authoring
- When existing user stories or issue descriptions are producing inconsistent agent output
page_texts.7:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-005-machine-readable-agent-specification-pattern.md#target-audience]

### Target Audience

This pattern is intended for:

- **Platform Engineers** designing agent pipeline infrastructure and issue tracker templates
- **Solutions Architects** defining the interface contract between human-authored work and AI agent execution
- **Engineering Leads** establishing team conventions for AI-executable work item authoring
- **Product Owners** authoring work items that will be fulfilled by AI agents rather than, or in addition to, human developers
page_texts.8:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-005-machine-readable-agent-specification-pattern.md#benefits]

### Benefits

- **Deterministic agent context**: Required sections eliminate the ambiguity that causes agent output to vary across similar tasks
- **Human-machine duality**: A single artifact serves both the human review workflow (readable prose) and the agent pipeline (parseable structure)
- **Reusable authoring standard**: Once established, the template is used across all agent types — implementation, documentation, testing, infrastructure — with domain-specific constraint references as the only variation
- **Quality gate foundation**: Structural validation (the first stage of the agent dispatch pipeline) can verify spec completeness programmatically because the required sections are known and fixed

page_texts.10:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-005-machine-readable-agent-specification-pattern.md#business-context]

### Business Context

The [AI Agent-Driven SDLC Strategy](../../../strategy/white-papers/engineering/ai-agent-sdlc-execution-model.md) establishes that AI agents participating in the SDLC require a specification format that is structured enough for deterministic parsing yet lightweight enough for product owners and engineers to author without a specialized tool or schema editor. The specification is the primary interface between the human-governed planning layer and the agent-executed delivery layer — its quality directly determines the quality of agent output.
page_texts.11:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-005-machine-readable-agent-specification-pattern.md#technical-context]

### Technical Context

AI agents operating in a pipeline receive a context window: a block of text assembled from the issue body, any attached files, and injected enterprise context (standards references, Golden Path catalog, constraints). The agent's model interprets this context to determine what to build, what constraints to respect, and how success is defined. A context window containing a well-formed spec — explicit goal, measurable acceptance criteria, named constraints — leaves no gap for the model to fill with assumptions from training data. A context window containing a loosely written issue description leaves many gaps, which the model fills with general knowledge that may not reflect enterprise standards.
page_texts.12:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-005-machine-readable-agent-specification-pattern.md#problem-details]

### Problem Details

Specific failure modes that this pattern addresses:

- **Ambiguous goal**: An issue titled "improve the API gateway" gives an agent no bounded scope — it may refactor interfaces, add rate limiting, update docs, or change configuration, depending on what its training data associates with "improve"
- **Unmeasurable acceptance criteria**: Without explicit, checkable criteria, an agent cannot self-validate its output and the reviewing engineer has no ground truth to evaluate against
- **Missing constraints**: Without explicit references to applicable standards, patterns, or file scope, the agent selects implementation approaches from its training distribution rather than from enterprise-approved choices
- **No enterprise work item link**: Without a reference to the governing work item in the enterprise system, the agent-executed task is invisible to sprint tracking and compliance audit
page_texts.13:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-005-machine-readable-agent-specification-pattern.md#forces-and-constraints]

### Forces and Constraints

- The template must be authorable by a product owner with no knowledge of AI prompt engineering — if it requires specialist skill to write, adoption will fail
- The template must be enforceable at authoring time via issue tracker template features, not reliant on post-hoc review
- The same template must serve multiple agent types (implementation, documentation, infrastructure, testing) — specialization is achieved through the Constraints section content, not template variation

page_texts.15:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-005-machine-readable-agent-specification-pattern.md#pattern-description]

### Pattern Description

The Machine-Readable Agent Specification Pattern consists of three mandatory structural components and one mandatory governance component, enforced via an issue tracker template:

| Section | Purpose | Agent Use |
|---|---|---|
| **Goal** | One-sentence bounded statement of what the agent must accomplish | Sets the scope boundary — the agent must not act outside it |
| **Acceptance Criteria** | Numbered, checkable list of measurable outcomes | The agent uses this as the self-validation checklist before producing output |
| **Constraints** | Explicit references to standards, patterns, files, or scope limits that govern the implementation | Replaces model training-data defaults with enterprise-approved choices |
| **Enterprise Work Item Reference** | Cross-reference to the governing work item in the enterprise system (e.g., `WI#1234`) | Enables the validation gate to enforce traceability before agent invocation |

[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-005-machine-readable-agent-specification-pattern.md#architecture-diagram]

### Architecture Diagram

```
[Machine-Readable Agent Specification — Anatomy]

Issue Tracker Template
        │
        ├── ## Goal                          (Required — 1 sentence, bounded scope)
        │   └── "Add request rate limiting to the API gateway component."
        │
        ├── ## Acceptance Criteria           (Required — checkable list)
        │   ├── - [ ] Rate limiting config added per standards/application/api-standards.md
        │   ├── - [ ] Unit tests cover the new limiting logic (≥ 90% branch coverage)
        │   └── - [ ] ADR updated to document rate limit values
        │
        ├── ## Constraints                   (Required — explicit references)
        │   ├── Follow: standards/application/api-standards.md § Rate Limiting
        │   ├── Target: components/api-gateway/src/
        │   └── Do not modify: components/api-gateway/src/auth/
        │
        └── ## Enterprise Work Item          (Required — governance link)
            └── WI#4821
                    │
                    ▼
        ┌──────────────────────┐
        │  Validation Gate     │  (PTN-TEC-AI-002)
        │  - All sections?     │
        │  - WI# present?      │
        └──────────┬───────────┘
                   │ Pass
                   ▼
        ┌──────────────────────┐
        │  Agent Context       │
        │  Window Assembly     │
        │  (spec + enterprise  │
        │   context injected)  │
        └──────────────────────┘
```
page_texts.17:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-005-machine-readable-agent-specification-pattern.md#template-definition]

### Template Definition

The canonical issue tracker template for an agent-executable specification:

```markdown
---
name: Agent Task
about: Specification for an autonomous AI agent execution task
title: "[AGENT] "
labels: agent-task
assignees: ''
---

## Goal

<!-- One sentence. What should the agent accomplish? Be specific and bounded. -->


## Acceptance Criteria

<!-- Checkable items. How will we know the task is complete? -->

- [ ]
- [ ]
- [ ]

## Constraints

<!-- What standards, patterns, files, or boundaries govern this task? -->

- Follow:
- Target:
- Do not modify:

## Enterprise Work Item

<!-- Required. Cross-reference to the governing work item (e.g., WI#1234, AB#1234). -->

WI#
```
page_texts.18:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-005-machine-readable-agent-specification-pattern.md#required-section-rules]

### Required Section Rules

**Goal**
- Must be a single sentence
- Must name the specific component, file, or system scope
- Must use an action verb (Add, Update, Remove, Generate, Implement)
- Must NOT be a question, a business outcome statement, or a multi-sentence description

**Acceptance Criteria**
- Each criterion must be independently verifiable — a reviewer can check each item without ambiguity
- Minimum 2 criteria; no practical maximum
- Must include at least one criterion that references a testable technical outcome (test coverage, validation result, lint pass)
- Must NOT include process steps ("developer reviews the PR") — only output states

**Constraints**
- Each constraint must reference a specific, locatable resource: a standards document section, a file path, a pattern ID, or a named boundary
- Must include at minimum: the applicable standard or pattern reference, and the target scope
- Must NOT contain generic statements ("follow best practices," "use secure coding") — these add no agent context

**Enterprise Work Item Reference**
- Must be present and contain a valid work item identifier
- Format is system-dependent: `WI#<id>` (Azure DevOps), `AB#<id>` (GitHub/ADO cross-reference), `JIRA-<key>`, etc.
- This field is validated by the pipeline gate and will block agent invocation if absent or malformed

[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-005-machine-readable-agent-specification-pattern.md#step-1--deploy-the-issue-tracker-template]

### Step 1 — Deploy the Issue Tracker Template

Store the template as `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/agent-task.md` (GitHub) or the equivalent for your issue tracker platform. Enabling the template ensures the structure is presented to spec authors at creation time without requiring them to remember the format.
page_texts.21:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-005-machine-readable-agent-specification-pattern.md#step-2--define-the-label-taxonomy]

### Step 2 — Define the Label Taxonomy

The `agent-task` label is the minimum required label to identify an agent-executable spec. Secondary labels enable routing to specialized agent pipelines (see PTN-TEC-AI-002). Define labels before deploying the dispatch pipeline:

| Label | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `agent-task` | Primary execution queue marker — all agent specs carry this label |
| `agent:implementation` | Route to the code implementation agent |
| `agent:documentation` | Route to the documentation generation agent |
| `agent:testing` | Route to the test generation agent |
| `agent:infrastructure` | Route to the infrastructure provisioning agent |
page_texts.22:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-005-machine-readable-agent-specification-pattern.md#step-3--train-spec-authors]

### Step 3 — Train Spec Authors

The spec template is only as good as the content that fills it. Engineers and product owners writing agent-executable specs need to understand:

- The Goal section is a scope constraint, not a business outcome statement — it must be precise enough for an agent to know when it has exceeded its mandate
- Acceptance Criteria are the agent's self-check list — vague criteria produce unverifiable output
- The Constraints section replaces the enterprise context an experienced engineer carries in their head — every applicable standard must be explicitly named

Run a brief authoring workshop using before/after examples. A well-formed spec alongside a poorly-formed one makes the standard immediately tangible.
page_texts.23:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-005-machine-readable-agent-specification-pattern.md#step-4--pilot-on-low-risk-tasks]

### Step 4 — Pilot on Low-Risk Tasks

Before enabling automated agent dispatch (PTN-TEC-AI-002), run 5–10 agent tasks manually:
1. Author a spec using the template
2. Manually invoke the agent with the spec as context
3. Evaluate the output against the Acceptance Criteria
4. Note which criteria were missed and trace back to spec ambiguity

Use pilot results to refine the Constraints section conventions for your specific domain. The spec template is a living standard — update it as the team accumulates evidence of what context agents actually need.
page_texts.24:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-005-machine-readable-agent-specification-pattern.md#step-5--version-the-template]

### Step 5 — Version the Template

Treat the spec template as a versioned artifact. As the team learns what context patterns produce the best agent output, update the template and record the change. This creates an organizational learning loop: better specs produce better output, and template versions provide a lens for explaining output quality changes over time.

---
page_texts.26:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-005-machine-readable-agent-specification-pattern.md#traceability]

### Traceability

Every agent-executable spec must contain an enterprise work item reference (the `## Enterprise Work Item` section). This reference is the single link that connects agent-executed delivery work to the sprint-governed, compliance-auditable record in the enterprise work management system. Without it, agent-generated pull requests are invisible to stakeholder reporting, sprint velocity metrics, and compliance audit trails.

The enterprise work item reference is validated by the pipeline dispatch gate (PTN-TEC-AI-002) as a hard prerequisite — no agent invocation fires without a valid reference present in the spec.
page_texts.27:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-005-machine-readable-agent-specification-pattern.md#sensitive-data-prohibition]

### Sensitive Data Prohibition

Issue tracker content is not an appropriate store for sensitive or regulated data. Specs authored using this template must not contain:

- Protected Health Information (PHI) or Personally Identifiable Information (PII)
- Security credentials, tokens, or connection strings
- Non-public business data or customer-identifiable information

The issue tracker is the execution surface; the enterprise work management system is the regulated record. If a task requires context that cannot appear in the issue tracker, that context must be injected at pipeline runtime from a secrets management system, not embedded in the spec.
page_texts.28:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-005-machine-readable-agent-specification-pattern.md#prompt-injection-risk]

### Prompt Injection Risk

Issue body content is untrusted user input. Because the spec body is passed directly to an AI model as context, maliciously crafted spec content could attempt to redirect agent behavior (prompt injection). The pipeline validation gate (PTN-TEC-AI-002) must sanitize issue body content before passing it to the model. Issue body content must never be executed as shell commands or passed to interpreters without sanitization.
page_texts.29:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-005-machine-readable-agent-specification-pattern.md#spec-quality-auditing]

### Spec Quality Auditing

Teams operating agent pipelines should track spec validation failure rate as an ongoing metric — the percentage of `agent-task` issues that fail structural validation before reaching the agent. A rising failure rate indicates spec authoring practice is degrading and the authoring standard needs reinforcement.

[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-005-machine-readable-agent-specification-pattern.md#example-1--implementation-task-well-formed]

### Example 1 — Implementation Task (Well-formed)

```markdown
## Goal
Add request rate limiting to the API gateway component to prevent abuse of public-facing endpoints.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Rate limiting middleware added to components/api-gateway/src/middleware/
- [ ] Default limits (100 req/min per client IP) configurable via environment variable
- [ ] Unit tests achieve ≥ 90% branch coverage on rate limiting logic
- [ ] standards/application/api-standards.md § 4.2 Rate Limiting requirements satisfied

## Constraints
- Follow: standards/application/api-standards.md § 4.2 Rate Limiting
- Follow: patterns/application/api-microservices/ middleware patterns
- Target: components/api-gateway/src/middleware/
- Do not modify: components/api-gateway/src/auth/

## Enterprise Work Item
WI#4821
```
page_texts.32:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-005-machine-readable-agent-specification-pattern.md#example-2--documentation-task-well-formed]

### Example 2 — Documentation Task (Well-formed)

```markdown
## Goal
Generate the API reference documentation for the claims-processor service's public REST endpoints.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] OpenAPI spec generated from source annotations in components/claims-processor/src/api/
- [ ] Generated docs published to docs/api/claims-processor.md
- [ ] All endpoints, request/response schemas, and error codes documented
- [ ] Links to relevant ADRs and standards included per documentation standards

## Constraints
- Follow: standards/application/api-standards.md § API Documentation
- Source: components/claims-processor/src/api/
- Target: docs/api/claims-processor.md

## Enterprise Work Item
WI#4899
```
page_texts.33:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-005-machine-readable-agent-specification-pattern.md#example-3--anti-pattern-poorly-formed-do-not-use]

### Example 3 — Anti-Pattern (Poorly-formed, do not use)

```markdown
## Goal
Improve the claims processing service.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Code is clean
- [ ] Tests pass

## Constraints
- Follow best practices

## Enterprise Work Item
(to be added)
```

> This spec will fail validation (WI# missing) and would produce non-deterministic agent output even if it passed. The Goal has no bounded scope, the Acceptance Criteria are not independently verifiable, and the Constraints reference no specific resource.

[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-005-machine-readable-agent-specification-pattern.md#tldr]

## TL;DR

**Problem**: AI agents produce non-deterministic output when given loosely structured human-authored work items because they fill specification gaps with training-data assumptions rather than enterprise standards.

**Solution**: A structured issue tracker template with three required sections (Goal, Acceptance Criteria, Constraints) and a mandatory enterprise work item reference. The template is deployed as an issue tracker template to enforce the structure at authoring time.

**Key Rule**: Goal = one bounded sentence. Acceptance Criteria = independently checkable outcomes. Constraints = explicitly named standards, patterns, and file scope. Enterprise Work Item = required; blocks agent invocation if absent.

**Where it fits**: This pattern defines the *input contract* for agent pipelines. PTN-TEC-AI-002 consumes it. PTN-GOV-AI-007 enforces the governance link it contains.
